stemMd: The shift-worker example illustrates which general claim?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All working-hour programmes are intentionally discriminatory.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Shift workers are less committed to learning.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Workshop skills are irrelevant to eligibility.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Equal probability of receiving an opportunity need not mean equal practical ability to benefit from it.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Random selection always favors flexible workers in the draw.

explanationMd: The example holds selection chances constant while varying the ability to attend. It demonstrates a difference between formal allocation equality and practical access without claiming biased randomization or discriminatory intent.

distractorRationale.c: The example does not address skill requirements.
distractorRationale.b: The example concerns schedules, not commitment.
